Hi Emma — great questions, and thanks for sending the data map. I summarized options below and proposed next steps so we can move quickly.

Quick summary of options (high level):

1) 0-retention (no request/response logs persisted):
   - Available on Redwood Private and on a Dedicated reserved pool with strict ACLs.
   - For hosted API we can offer an ephemeral mode for certain routes where we avoid writing request/response bodies to long-term logs, but operational traces and aggregated metrics still exist for SLOs.
   - Requires an exception in the contract and an operational runbook; typically a security review + acceptance of limited observability.

2) Shortened logs / custom schedule:
   - We can implement route-level retention windows (e.g., 0 days for /payments, 30 days for others) with a config change and minor onboarding work.
   - There is a small engineering and billing uplift for custom schedules; we will include options in the proposal.

3) Encryption & residency controls:
   - KMS-backed keys for stored artifacts, and VPC/Private deployment options for data residency concerns.

Next steps I propose:
- Rafael and Marissa to review the data map (attached) and confirm feasibility for per-route 0-retention and estimated dev effort.
- We prepare a short proposal (technical approach + contract language + cost delta) for your legal and security.
- Optional 30-min tech sync with Liam to resolve any infra-level questions.

Rafael/Marissa — any obvious red flags from an implementation standpoint?

Thanks,

Hi Emma / Liam — looping in a couple technical details so you have a clearer picture ahead of a sync. I quoted Camila's summary below for context.

On Mon, Jul 20, 2026 at 4:10 PM Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick summary of options (high level):

> 1) 0-retention (no request/response logs persisted):
>    - Available on Redwood Private and on a Dedicated reserved pool with strict ACLs.
>    - For hosted API we can offer an ephemeral mode for certain routes where we avoid writing request/response bodies to long-term logs, but operational traces and aggregated metrics still exist for SLOs.

Technical feasibility notes:
- 0-retention true (no request/response persisted) is achievable only when you control the serving boundary (Private or Dedicated). For our hosted environment we can approximate but cannot guarantee zero telemetry; traces and short-lived buffers are used for debugging and autoscaling.
- Per-route retention: we already have a config layer that supports route-level retention toggles; implementing this for the routes you listed in the data map is straightforward but requires validation and a short QA window (estimated 2-3 weeks of engineering effort + onboarding).
- Audit & contract language: we'll include explicit language that confirms request/response bodies are not persisted and describe the exceptions (e.g., catastrophic incident investigations where ephemeral buffers may be captured under an approved legal process). SOC 2 scope remains compatible; we will surface control descriptions.
- Security controls: KMS for at-rest artifacts, HSM options for Private customers, and VPC-only connections for data egress control.

Pricing/ops impact:
- 0-retention on Private: included as part of the Private license (platform + support).
- Hosted 0-retention approximation / per-route short retention: normally a one-time onboarding fee + 8-12% ongoing premium tied to custom retention policies. We will put specific numbers in the proposal.

Next steps (technical):
- Rafael will prepare a scoped SOW with timeline and cost outline.
- Camila will prepare contract language for the legal team to review.
- Let's schedule a 30-min technical sync. Camila — can you propose 2 times? Emma/Liam — which timezone is easiest?

Thanks,
